The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- Small, dark/black round spots scattered across the green leaf blade
- Larger dark lesions along the midrib/central vein area
- Some spots appear raised/embedded

Top candidates: **Tar_spot** (raised black stromata on leaf) and **Physoderma_brown_spot** (small spots on blade + dark midrib lesions). Let me compare reference images.
The Tar_spot reference closely matches the test image pattern. Let me also check Southern_rust and Common_rust to rule them out, and look more carefully at the midrib detail.

Rust is ruled out (orange/red pustules vs. black spots in test image). The test image has black spots on the blade AND dark elongated lesions on the midrib — a dual pattern. Let me check a few more candidates.

Eyespot and Holcus_spot are ruled out (yellow/tan halos, large white spots — don't match).

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: small dark/black circular spots scattered on the green leaf blade + elongated dark lesions concentrated along the midrib
- **Physoderma_brown_spot** describes exactly this dual pattern: "small tan/yellow lesions on blade + dark brown to black oval spots on midrib"
- **Tar_spot** shows scattered black raised stromata but no specific midrib concentration pattern
- Rust (Common/Southern) ruled out — orange/red pustules, not black spots
- Eyespot/Holcus_spot ruled out — wrong morphology

The **midrib lesions** are the key distinguishing feature: concentrated, elongated, dark lesions on the midrib is the hallmark of Physoderma_brown_spot ("dark purplish to black oval spots also occur on the midrib"). The blade spots, while darker than the classic "yellowish to brown" description, match the small round lesion pattern. The Physoderma reference (bottom-right panel) also shows dark spots clustering near the midrib, closely matching the test image.
